evidence: The amendment's distinctive content is 'pointer-swap target', 'retire-when-idle', 'atomic nginx-upstream flip', and the 'bug-7b4a saturation rationale' — none of which the current pattern requires to match.
findings.finding: AC2's proving grep `grep -i 'mcp\|blue-green'` on the 0079 file can pass on a pre-existing incidental 'mcp' mention without the new amendment actually being added, since 'mcp' is an unanchored common substring.
scenarios: ADR 0079 already contains the word 'mcp' somewhere unrelated; the grep passes green while the required amendment text was never written.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State in the new ADR that per-client bearer PATs follow the established static-verifier secret contract (server holds SHA-256 digests only, env-var NAMES in config, sourced via the SSM->0600 .env substrate of ADR 0008, never logged), and note where PAT issuance/rotation/revocation is owned.
evidence: Plan: "each client (copilot/codex/claude) presents its own bearer PAT in the Authorization header" — a new credential on the internet-reachable path
AC3 names transport/http_tls_at_edge/allowed hosts+origins/auth_resource_server_url/verifier static but NOT the PAT secret source
ADR 0050 consequences: "Secrets are never in config (only env-var names) and never logged; static tokens hold only digests" — establishes the contract the new ADR should cross-reference
ADR 0008: box secrets are SSM SecureString -> ephemeral 0600 .env, no static creds — the substrate the PATs would use
findings.finding: The plan introduces a new boundary-crossing credential class — per-client bearer PATs presented over the internet-reachable nginx /mcp/ edge — but decision #1 and the config-key acceptance criterion never name where those PAT secrets (server-side static-verifier digests / env-var token source) are provisioned, stored, or rotated on the box. ADR 0050 binds static mode to digests-only/env-var-names/never-logged and ADR 0008 gives the box an SSM-SecureString->0600 .env substrate, so this is a decision-record completeness gap, not a plaintext-secret defect.
findings.location: Decisions #1 (Exposure + auth) and Acceptance Criteria bullet 3 (named config keys)
scenarios: An implementer of the secrets slice picks an ad-hoc PAT storage/issuance path (e.g. plaintext in compose config) because the ADR left the PAT lifecycle unstated
PAT rotation/revocation has no owning decision, so a leaked client PAT has no documented revocation procedure
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to Decision #1 (and a config-key to AC3) cross-referencing ADR 0050 (digests-only/env-var-name/never-logged) and ADR 0008 (SSM SecureString -> ephemeral 0600 .env), naming the PAT secret source and rotation path so the secrets slice cannot introduce plaintext PATs on the /mcp/ path.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin the capability claim in ADR §1 to the specific client surface + version verified (e.g. Claude Code CLI --header, Codex config.toml, Copilot CLI) and note the known caveats (Copilot CLI OAuth-discovery-then-Bearer behaviour; Claude.ai web connector static_headers/beta) so the static-mode choice is grounded, not asserted.
evidence: Plan quote: 'research confirmed all three clients support a static Authorization: Bearer <token> header for remote HTTP MCP and none require OAuth, so static is the minimal mode that satisfies all three clients.'

Retrieved: github anthropics/claude-ai-mcp#112 reports the Claude.ai Advanced-settings UI exposes only OAuth client id/secret with no Bearer field; claude.com connector docs state static bearer tokens are 'supported in beta through request headers (static_headers)'.
Retrieved: github github/copilot-cli#3100 'HTTP MCP server with Bearer token fails OAuth ...' — workaround is manually /mcp enable to bypass OAuth discovery.

Retrieved: truefoundry.com and Claude Code docs confirm the Claude Code CLI supports `claude mcp add --transport http --header "Authorization: Bearer ..."`, so the assertion holds for the CLI surface but not uniformly across desktop/web.
findings.finding: The ADR's load-bearing capability assertion — 'all three clients (copilot/codex/claude) support a static Authorization: Bearer header for remote HTTP MCP and none require OAuth' — is stated flatly without pinning the concrete client surface/version tested, but retrieved public sources show it is nuanced per surface (Claude.ai connector UI reportedly exposes only OAuth fields with static bearer in beta via static_headers; GitHub Copilot CLI has an open bug where Bearer HTTP MCP fails OAuth discovery and needs a manual /mcp enable workaround).
scenarios: A client (e.g. Copilot CLI or Claude.ai web connector) attempts OAuth discovery against the static verifier and fails to connect, or the desktop UI offers no Bearer-header field, blocking the dogfooding goal the ADR is written to enable.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short 'client support evidence' note to Decision §1 citing the exact configuration mechanism per client (Claude Code CLI `--header "Authorization: Bearer"`; Codex config.toml MCP http headers; Copilot CLI header + the /mcp enable caveat) and the surface/version tested, and state explicitly which surfaces (CLI vs desktop/web) the static-bearer decision covers.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Record the evidence class for the per-client static-bearer capability (Claude = grounded in mcp-auth.md §4; Copilot/Codex = unverified 'research') with a citable source per client, or route a small SPIKE to confirm Copilot & Codex accept a static `Authorization: Bearer` header for remote HTTP MCP before the client-config slice commits to `static` for all three.
evidence: Plan quote: 'research confirmed all three clients (copilot/codex/claude) support a static `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header for remote HTTP MCP and none require OAuth, so `static` is the minimal mode that satisfies all three clients'
docs/mcp-auth.md:183-184 grounds static bearer ONLY for Claude: 'Static bearer — Claude Code --header "Authorization: Bearer <token>" / Claude.ai static_headers; pairs with the static verifier.'

ABSENCE: no repo doc (searched 'copilot', 'codex' under docs/) confirms Copilot/Codex remote-MCP static-header support; the claim is Partially-verified (Claude=Verified surface; Copilot/Codex=Unverified surface)

The 'static' verifier mode itself exists and is grounded (docs/mcp-auth.md:87-90, src/rebar/_mcp_auth.py), so the rebar-side surface is Verified — the gap is only the client-side capability for two of three clients
findings.finding: The auth decision rests on an external client-capability claim — that GitHub Copilot and OpenAI Codex (not just Claude) accept a static `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header for remote HTTP MCP and require no OAuth — that is stated from uncited 'research' and is not grounded in any existing repo doc; rebar's own docs/mcp-auth.md §4 documents the static-bearer path only for Claude Code / Claude.ai.
findings.location: Decisions §1 (Exposure + auth): 'research confirmed all three clients support a static Authorization: Bearer header ... and none require OAuth'
scenarios: The client-config slice wires Copilot/Codex against the static-bearer edge and one of them turns out to require OAuth/DCR or a non-standard header, invalidating the 'static is the minimal mode that satisfies all three' rationale after the ADR is Accepted
findings.suggested_fix: In Decision §1, replace the bare 'research confirmed all three clients' with a per-client citation (link each client's remote-MCP header/auth docs) and mark Copilot/Codex as to-be-verified by the client-config slice or a preceding spike; keep the Claude claim tied to mcp-auth.md §4.
